name: Art-Siadziba
watch: Founded 24 Dec 2011 by Stas Babaitsau, Franak Viačorka, Zmicier Afanasenka and Pavel Belavus to promote Belarusian-language culture among the young; moved repeatedly after evictions (Horizont club, Pushkin Ave 28a, an underground flat, Instrumentalnaya 6 from Oct 2013). Map point is approximate, near the last premises.
records_note: Liquidated on 23 July 2021; its site artsiadziba.by returned no content, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked.

name: Art Sonje Center
watch: Private non-profit contemporary kunsthalle in Seoul founded by Chung Hee-ja.
records_note: Its site posts no annual reports, accounts, sponsor names or board; it links the Daewoo Foundation and invites corporate sponsors only.

name: Artbank
funding: Commonwealth art-leasing programme inside a federal department. Government funding ended in 1992; leasing income pays for operations and acquisitions.
records_note: Publishes yearly reviews for 2024 and 2025, funds itself by leasing art, names no sponsors, and reports accounts through its parent department.

name: Artium Museoa
funding: Basque public museum funded mainly by the Álava provincial council.
records_note: It posts activity reports 2019 to 2025, audited accounts 2019 to 2025, sponsor logos without dates, and names its Patronato.

name: Artizon Museum
funding: Run by the Ishibashi Foundation, set up in 1956 by Bridgestone founder Shojiro Ishibashi, who gave it his art collection. Known as the Bridgestone Museum of Art before.
watch: Bridgestone's Firestone unit was sued in 2005 over child labour on its Liberian plantation; the Seventh Circuit ruled for Firestone in 2011.
records_note: The Ishibashi Foundation, Artizon's operator, posts reports from 2019, balance sheets for 2020 to 2025 and a dated officer list, but no donor list.

name: Artpace San Antonio
funding: The Linda Pace Foundation endowment, National Endowment for the Arts, Texas Commission on the Arts; 501(c)(3) non-profit.

name: Artspace Sydney
funding: Create NSW, Creative Australia (Australia Council), City of Sydney; registered non-profit visual arts organization.
watch: Independent non-profit kunsthalle in the historic Gunnery, Woolloomooloo, with 10 rent-free artist studios.

name: Artspeak
funding: Canada Council for the Arts, BC Arts Council, City of Vancouver; registered non-profit charity.

name: Asia Art Archive (AAA)
funding: Individuals, foundations, corporate patrons, HK government agencies and an annual auction; the US arm cites NYSCA, NYC DCLA and the Ruth Foundation.
records_note: The archive names its donors by tier and lists its board, but the site refused direct access so reports and accounts stay unchecked.

name: Associação Núcleo de Arte
funding: Artists' association with over 100 members. State funding ended in the civil war; a late-1990s profile names Hivos as donor. No current funder list is published.
watch: Official foundation 1948; reopened in 1993 by young artists. Maputo's council and the CTA led a 2021 mural project with 40 of its members.
records_note: The association's only page found is a late-1990s profile naming Hivos; it publishes no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Atlanta Contemporary
funding: $0.84M expenses (FY2023); Warhol and Ruth foundations, City of Atlanta, Fulton County, Arthur M. Blank family fund, Intuit, members.
watch: In-kind sponsors include Post Meridiem Spirit Co (alcohol) and Orange Barrel Media (advertising). Leadership turnover 2025-26, no funder controversy.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, a FY26 donors page names funders, and the board is listed.

name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
funding: 497,998 visitors (2024-25). Run by Tātaki Auckland Unlimited for Auckland Council. Partners include BMW, Van Cleef & Arpels, HSBC, Anthony Harper, Baker Tilly; trusts include Chartwell and Mackelvie.
watch: HSBC backed A Century of Modern Art in 2025. HSBC agreed a $1.92 billion US penalty in December 2012 over money-laundering failures.
records_note: Parent Tataki Auckland Unlimited posts audited annual reports 2021 to 2026 and its board; the gallery's own 2024-25 review names partners and trusts.
